summary: Red team of the accepted new roadmap EllipticCurveModularityImaginaryQuadratic (Caraiani–Newton §§6–7). The final theorems and every layer statement match CN's Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 6.1 and 7.1 and Corollaries 6.1.1, 6.1.2 and 7.1.2. All explicit arithmetic in the packet, re-checked exactly, is correct. The 15 Mathlib baseline citations hold, and the suggested file compiles at the pins with sorry as its only warning. The weaknesses are in the prerequisite closure and in reuse. The theorem that the twisted curve Y_ρ̄ is rational (Shepherd-Barron–Taylor), which the switching step needs, is planned nowhere (high). CN Lemma 6.2.2 and Allen–Newton Lemma 2.3 are requested from R01.4, which excludes decomposed-genericity results, and have no owner. The Q-curve step ignores the now-accepted GT.6/quadratic-q-curves-modular, and the real-quadratic branches lean on an unowned FLHS theorem nothing needs. The modularity predicate is posed over all number fields, where r_{π,ι} does not exist. AKT Theorem 8.1 is requested although CL.9/thm-5-2 covers every instance used. The X₀(3)/X₀(5) j-maps duplicate EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons EC.5. Tau Ceti's Mordell–Weil, shortCurve and quadraticTwist declarations are not reused. The suggested file states none of the 43 theorems. Four low findings cover tests, source issues, a duplicate in ML.1 and timeless writing. Totals: 1 high, 8 medium, 5 low.

findings.claim: The switching argument needs the theorem that the twisted modular curve Y_ρ̄ (p = 3, 5, cyclotomic determinant) is isomorphic over the base field to an open subscheme of ℙ¹, so that it has points to which Hilbert irreducibility and weak approximation apply. No node plans this. hilbert-local-selection starts from 'After solvable_preparation has made Yρ̄ an open subcurve of ℙ¹L', but solvable_preparation's statement contains no such conclusion. symplectic-twist deliberately states only geometric genus zero and makes rationality conditional on an F-point that nothing supplies. Upstream ModularCurves 5C (over ℚ) stops at a smooth, geometrically irreducible affine curve. Without this input the prerequisite chain of switch_five and switch_three (hence of CN Theorem 6.1, Theorem 7.1 and Theorems 1.1–1.2) does not close.
findings.evidence: Caraiani–Newton, arXiv:2301.10509v3 (27 March 2025; sha256 57abc79a…fd0c3, read 2026-10-09), proof of Proposition 6.1.5, p.89: 'Now we apply [AKT23, Lemma 9.7] in the same way as in the proof of [AKT23, Proposition 9.13] to find an L-rational point of the modular curve Yρ corresponding to a modular elliptic curve E/L. The curve Yρ is isomorphic to an open subset of the projective line over F. Combining Hilbert irreducibility, in the form of [Ser08, Theorem 3.5.3], and weak approximation for the projective line, we can find points in Yρ(L) that avoid a thin subset'. Allen–Khare–Thorne, arXiv:1910.12986v2 (2 September 2022; sha256 230de16e…4b44, read 2026-10-09), proof of Lemma 9.7, p.75: 'There is an isomorphism between Yρ and an open subset of the projective line over K. This is [SBT97, Lemma 1.1] when p = 5, and the same reference explains how the same proof works in the case p = 3. In particular, Yρ has infinitely many K-rational points.' Packet: IQ.2/hilbert-local-selection statement 'After solvable_preparation has made Yρ̄ an open subcurve of ℙ¹L, …'. IQ.2/solvable-preparation statement, in full, concludes only: 'There is a finite Galois solvable CM extension L/F disjoint from Favoid such that each w|2,3,p is split over L⁺ and ρ̄|GLw is trivial; for every w|p there are local elliptic curves with good ordinary and good supersingular reduction and rational p-torsion; Lw(√−1)/Lw is unramified at w|2; a rational prime q>5 witnessing decomposed genericity splits completely in L.' IQ.2/symplectic-twist: proof step 'Use genus zero at levels 3 and 5, keeping existence of an F-point separate from geometric rationality'; API symplecticTwist.rational 'If the smooth completion has an F-point, its genus-zero curve is F-isomorphic to ℙ¹'. The prerequisites of hilbert-local-selection (symplectic-twist, solvable-preparation, GlobalNumberFields layer 1, IG.2, EllipticCurves layer 4) do not supply an F-point either. Upstream content/tau-ceti/ModularCurves/README.md:1279–1300 (§5C) constructs Y(ρ)/ℚ, 'a smooth affine curve Y(ρ)/ℚ, and establish its field-points description', plus conditional geometric irreducibility; it states no rationality and works over ℚ only. A search of every packet and roadmap under research/blueprint for 'Shepherd-Barron', 'SBT97' and the twisted-curve rationality statement finds only unrelated Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor citations.
findings.fix: Add to IQ.2 a theorem node, or a precise request to ModularCurvesPartII:R12.4 (twisted curves), stating: for p ∈ {3,5}, a field F of characteristic 0 and a continuous ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(𝔽_p) with det ρ̄ = ε̄_p, the smooth completion of Y_ρ̄ is F-isomorphic to ℙ¹_F. findings.claim: Two decomposed-genericity lemmas on the critical path have no owner anywhere in the atlas. (a) CN Lemma 6.2.2: over a quadratic field, absolute irreducibility on G_{F(ζp)} implies decomposed genericity. It turns CN Theorem 6.1 into Corollary 6.1.1, and so feeds Theorem 7.1 and Theorem 1.1. (b) Allen–Newton Lemma 2.3: over a Galois field, an image containing SL₂(𝔽₅) is decomposed generic. It feeds Theorem 1.2. The packet sends both to R01.4. But the accepted ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations packet plans CN 7.1.1 and 6.1.4 in R01.4, plans neither of these lemmas, and states that decomposed-genericity results are not stated there. PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5 and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.7, the owners it points to, do not contain them either.
findings.evidence: Caraiani–Newton, arXiv:2301.10509v3 (27 March 2025; sha256 57abc79a…fd0c3, read 2026-10-09), Corollary 6.1.1 proof, p.87: 'Combine Theorem 6.1 and Lemma 6.2.2.' Lemma 6.2.2, p.90: 'Let F/Q be a quadratic field, let p be an odd prime, and let ρ : GF → GL2(Fp) be a homomorphism. Suppose that ρ|GF(ζp) is absolutely irreducible. Then ρ is decomposed generic.' Corollary 6.1.2 proof, p.87: 'It follows from [AN20, Lemma 2.3] that, if F/Q is finite Galois and E/F is an elliptic curve such that the image of rE,5 contains SL2(F5), then rE,5 is decomposed generic.' Packet: IQ.3/quadratic-modularity proof step 'Import the quadratic-field genericity lemma from the residual-image owner', with prerequisite ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4. Request #13: 'CN Lemma 6.2.2 … Also Allen–Newton Lemma 2.3 … Import these group/genericity results rather than planning them here.' ownership.excludes: 'General residual-image/genericity classification'. Accepted research/blueprint/packets/ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.json: R01.4/restriction-to-the-cyclotomic-field cites CN only at 'Lemma 7.1.1, p. 92 of arXiv v3' and 'Lemma 6.1.4, p. 88 of arXiv v3'. Its items (b), (c) and (f) are CN 7.1.1 and 6.1.4; no item is 6.2.2. Node G7/taylor-wiles-image-lemmas, hypothesis: 'the decomposed-genericity halves of Lemmas 5.2.2, 5.2.4(1), 5.2.6(1) and of Allen et al. Lemmas 7.1.5, 7.1.6(3)–(5), 7.1.7 are not stated here (they belong to PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.5)'. The PA.5 nodes of research/blueprint/packets/PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure.json (genericity-normal-closure-restriction = ACC+ Lemma 7.1.7, split-test-prime-image-preservation, …) and the AG2.7 nodes of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII--AG2.6.json (completely-split-generic-prime, existential-decomposed-genericity, infinitely-many-decomposed-generic-primes, genericity-transfer-and-projective-qualification) contain neither statement. No packet cites Allen–Newton 'Monodromy for some rank two Galois representations over CM fields' (arXiv:1901.05490). The baseline already has CN Lemma 6.2.1 (Goursat): Mathlib/GroupTheory/Goursat.lean:104, Subgroup.goursat_surjective.

findings.claim: The modularity predicate is defined for an arbitrary number field F through the Galois representation r_{π,ι} attached to a cuspidal regular algebraic π on GL₂(𝔸_F). The supplier AG2 constructs r_{π,ι} only over CM or totally real fields, and for a general number field no such representation is known to exist. As stated, the definition cannot be built. modularity_transport likewise claims invariance 'over any number field' and base change along any solvable extension, but its supplier PA.5 is stated only for CM or totally real fields. CN gives the Galois form of the definition only for imaginary CM F; for general F it uses the L-function form. Every consumer works over ℚ, a quadratic field or a solvable CM extension, so nothing requires the extra generality.
findings.evidence: Packet IQ.1/modular: 'For a number field F and a Weierstrass curve E/F with Δ(E) ≠ 0, Modular(E) means: … a cuspidal regular algebraic automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸F), cohomological of weight 0, such that rπ,ι≅rE,p∨'; hypotheses 'F is a number field.'; prerequisite AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7.
